A 38-year-old male college student arrives at the emergency department with several days of back pain
and fatigue. He recently returned from a study abroad trip to Morocco, where he participated in
activities such as swimming at the beach, eating local foods like couscous and bean salad, and riding a
camel in the desert. His vital signs include a temperature of 99°F (37°C), blood pressure of 129/83
mmHg, pulse of 65/min, and respirations of 8/min. He reports otherwise good health but notes
episodes of dark urine. On physical examination, his skin appears more yellow than usual, particularly
under his eyelids. Which of the following findings is most likely in this patient? Answer Choices: (A)
Absent urine bilirubin (B) Positive Coombs test (C) Increased direct bilirubin in serum (D) Decreased
urine urobilinogen (E) Conjugated hyperbilirubinemia (F) Increased serum haptoglobin levels (G)
Hemoglobinuria (H) Dark stools due to excess stercobilin (I) Elevated urine bilirubin (J) Increased
indirect bilirubin in serum
 A. Elevated urine bilirubin
B. Absent urine bilirubin
C. Dark stools due to excess stercobilin
D. Conjugated hyperbilirubinemia
E. Positive Coombs test
F. Decreased urine urobilinogen
G. Hemoglobinuria
H. Increased indirect bilirubin in serum

I. Increased serum haptoglobin levels
J. Increased direct bilirubin in serum
